	brte => Brute-force
		godns => Gobuster (DNS subdomain enumeration mode)
		dnscn => dnscan (DNS subdomain scanner)
		dirb0 => Dirb (A web content scanner)
		dnsmp => Dnsmap (Scan for subdomains using bruteforcing techniques)

		anubs => Anubis (Subdomain enumeration and information gathering tool)
		lepus => Lepus (Subdomain finder)
		dnsen => dnsenum (enumerates DNS information)

		nmaps => Nmap (Normal Nmap Scan)
		nikto => Nikto web server scanner
		dnsrc => DNSRecon (DNS Enumeration and Scanning Tool)
		dnscn => dnscan (DNS subdomain scanner)
		dirb0 => Dirb (A web content scanner)
		rusts => RustScan (The Modern Port Scanner)
		mstcp => TCP Scan by Metasploit
		cmsmp => CMS scanner that automates the process of detecting security flaws of the most popular CMSs
		jooms => OWASP JoomScan (Joomla Vulnerability Scanner)
		
	osnt => OSINT
		whois => Whois (Obtain Whois information and name server of a website)
		mstwb => Pulling urls from Archive.org by Metasploit
		dataf => Default File Check by DataSploit
		datag => Check Google PDF by DataSploit
		datad => Find DNS Records by DataSploit
		ghsdm => Goohost (Extracts hosts/subdomains for a specific domain with Google search)
		ghsip => Goohost (Extracts IP or emails for a specific domain with Google search)
		
	ssls => SSL
		ciphr => Cipherscan (Tests the ordering of the SSL/TLS ciphers on a given target)

service.description: Are you looking for an API that can quickly and easily download and parse sitemap.xml files into JSON format? Look no further! Our API allows you to make a simple GET request, passing in the URL of a sitemap.xml file as a parameter. The API will handle the rest, downloading the file, parsing it into a JSON object, and returning the result in the response. And if you need a little extra information to help organize and navigate the URLs in the sitemap, we've got you covered there too. By adding a query parameter to the GET request, you can also include category and breadcrumb information for each URL in the parsed sitemap. Give it a try and see how much easier working with sitemaps can be!
